result.topic_en: Statements (paragraphs 345-352) of quadratic reciprocity-type laws on when a number n or -n is a quadratic residue modulo primes of the form 4nq±d, together with the start of an attempted proof for prime divisors of the form 4nq+ii.
result.transcription:
Tractatus de numerorum doctrina Cap. 10. 43
Deinde etiam numerus positivus $+n$ erit residuum, si divisor primus fuerit formae $4nq-1$, vel generalius $4nq-ii$; pro his autem divisoribus numerus negativus $-n$ inter non-residua reperietur.
345. Si numerus positivus $n$ sit residuum pro divisore $d$, erit etiam residuum pro divisore primo quocunque formae $4nq\pm d$, vel adeo $4nq\pm dii$; at si numerus negativus $-n$ sit residuum pro divisore $d$, erit is quidem residuum pro divisore $4nq+d$, at non-residuum pro divisore $4nq-d$.
346. Si numerus positivus $n$ fuerit residuum pro divisore $d$, deinde etiam pro divisore $e$, erit etiam residuum pro divisore primo quocunque formae $4nq\pm de$. At si numerus negativus $-n$ fuerit residuum pro divisoribus $d$ et $e$, erit quoque residuum pro divisore quocunque primo formae $4nq+de$; pro divisoribus autem $4nq-de$ inter non-residua referetur.
347. Si numerus positivus $n$ fuerit non-residuum pro divisoribus $d$ et $e$, certe erit residuum pro divisoribus primis omnibus formae $4nq\pm de$; at si numerus negativus $-n$ sit non-residuum pro divisoribus $d$ et $e$, is erit residuum pro omnibus divisoribus primis formae $4nq+de$; pro divisoribus autem formae $4nq-de$ erit non-residuum.
348. Quicunque numerus $\pm n$ proponatur, erit is semper residuum, si divisor primus fuerit in aliqua talium formarum $4nq+A$, $4nq+B$, $4nq+C$, etc. contentus, quarum numerus aequatur semissi multitudinis numerorum ad $4n$ primorum eoque minorum. Sin autem divisor in reliquis formis contineatur, erit is non-residuum.
349. Hic autem excipi debent casus, quibus numerus $n$ est quadratus, quippe qui semper inter residua occurrit, quicunque divisores accipiantur. Ac si $n$ sit quadratum negativum, eadem ratio valet ac pro $-1$.
350. Primum igitur demonstrari debet, si divisor primus sit $4nq+ii$, existente $i$ numero impari, inter residua quadratorum semper occurrere tam numeros $n$ et $q$, quam eorum negativa $-n$ et $-q$. Sit $i=2m+1$, et quia divisor $4nq+4mm+4m+1$ est formae $4p+1$, inter residua continetur quadratum negativum $-4mm-4m-1$, ideoque numerus $4nq$, et ob $4$ residuum, etiam numerus $nq$, itemque $-nq$, quare vel ambo numeri $n$ et $q$ simul inter residua, vel ambo simul inter non-residua occurrere deberent, unde dum alteruter fuerit inter residua, et alter ibidem repe-
riatur necesse est.
351. Si $n$ non esset residuum, nullum daretur quadratum $xx$, ut $xx-n$ divisibile esset per $4nq+4mm+4m+1$. Si ergo demonstrari posset dari hujusmodi quadratum, evicta esset veritas propositionis. Vel si $n$ esset non-residuum, haec expressio $n^{2nq+2mm+2m}-1$ non esset divisibilis per numerum primum, quare si contrarium demonstrari posset, haberemus quod intendimus. (*)
352. Deinde si divisor primus sit $4nq-4mm-4m-1$, inter residua quadratorum occurrere numerum $n$, inter non-residua vero numerum $-n$, demonstrari oportet. Pari autem jure inter
(*) Script. ad marg. Si $n$ esset non-residuum, foret quoque non-residuum $nzz$, ideoque etiam
$\pm nzz \mp y(4nq+4mm+4m+1)$,
quae expressio, si uno saltem casu esset quadratum, propositum constaret. Quod ob signa ambigua semper uno saltem casu evenire debere videtur; idque eo magis, cum etiam $n$ et $q$ sint permutabiles, quin etiam verum est, etsi divisor non sit primus. Dubium, si $n=3$, $q=5$, $2m+1=5$, $\pm 3zz\pm 85y$, vel $\pm 5zz\pm 85y$ quadratum effici nequit. Ergo demonstratio ita est adornanda, ut divisor statuatur primus.

methods.what: Residue character of n and -n for primes 4nq-ii
methods.quote: numerus positivus $+n$ erit residuum, si divisor primus fuerit formae $4nq-1$, vel generalius $4nq-ii$; pro his autem divisoribus numerus negativus $-n$ inter non-residua reperietur.

methods.what: Residue character transfers from divisor d to primes 4nq±d (form of quadratic reciprocity)
methods.quote: Si numerus positivus $n$ sit residuum pro divisore $d$, erit etiam residuum pro divisore primo quocunque formae $4nq\pm d$, vel adeo $4nq\pm dii$

methods.what: Product rule for residues over two divisors d, e
methods.quote: erit etiam residuum pro divisore primo quocunque formae $4nq\pm de$

methods.what: Product of two non-residue characters gives residue
methods.quote: Si numerus positivus $n$ fuerit non-residuum pro divisoribus $d$ et $e$, certe erit residuum pro divisoribus primis omnibus formae $4nq\pm de$

methods.what: Exactly half of the residue classes mod 4n coprime to 4n give primes for which ±n is a residue
methods.quote: quarum numerus aequatur semissi multitudinis numerorum ad $4n$ primorum eoque minorum

methods.what: Reduction: modulo prime 4nq+ii, n and q have the same residue character, since -1 and 4 are residues
methods.quote: vel ambo numeri $n$ et $q$ simul inter residua, vel ambo simul inter non-residua occurrere deberent

methods.what: Euler's criterion formulation: n is a non-residue iff n^{(p-1)/2}-1 not divisible by p
methods.quote: haec expressio $n^{2nq+2mm+2m}-1$ non esset divisibilis per numerum primum

items.quote: Si numerus positivus $n$ sit residuum pro divisore $d$, erit etiam residuum pro divisore primo quocunque formae $4nq\pm d$
items.english: If the positive number n is a residue for divisor d, it will also be a residue for any prime divisor of the form 4nq±d.

items.quote: Quicunque numerus $\pm n$ proponatur, erit is semper residuum, si divisor primus fuerit in aliqua talium formarum $4nq+A$, $4nq+B$, $4nq+C$, etc. contentus, quarum numerus aequatur semissi multitudinis numerorum ad $4n$ primorum eoque minorum.
items.english: Whatever number ±n is proposed, it will always be a residue if the prime divisor is contained in one of the forms 4nq+A, 4nq+B, 4nq+C, etc., whose number equals half the count of numbers prime to 4n and less than it.

items.quote: Primum igitur demonstrari debet, si divisor primus sit $4nq+ii$, existente $i$ numero impari, inter residua quadratorum semper occurrere tam numeros $n$ et $q$, quam eorum negativa $-n$ et $-q$.
items.english: First therefore it must be proved that, if the prime divisor is 4nq+ii with i odd, both n and q, as well as their negatives -n and -q, always occur among the quadratic residues.

items.quote: Si ergo demonstrari posset dari hujusmodi quadratum, evicta esset veritas propositionis.
items.english: If therefore it could be proved that such a square exists, the truth of the proposition would be established.

items.quote: Deinde si divisor primus sit $4nq-4mm-4m-1$, inter residua quadratorum occurrere numerum $n$, inter non-residua vero numerum $-n$, demonstrari oportet.
items.english: Next, if the prime divisor is 4nq-4mm-4m-1, it must be proved that n occurs among the quadratic residues, but -n among the non-residues.

items.quote: Dubium, si $n=3$, $q=5$, $2m+1=5$, $\pm 3zz\pm 85y$, vel $\pm 5zz\pm 85y$ quadratum effici nequit.
items.english: Doubtful case: if n=3, q=5, 2m+1=5, ±3zz±85y or ±5zz±85y cannot be made a square.

items.quote: Ergo demonstratio ita est adornanda, ut divisor statuatur primus.
items.english: Therefore the proof must be arranged so that the divisor is taken to be prime.
